rendered.overview: This Colorless deck led by [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] ramps hard into big colorless spells so double cascade triggers chain into more cascades and free spells. [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] together make infinite colorless mana with no mana cost to run, fueling repeated activations. The backup plan is grinding value off artifacts, Eldrazi, and Ugin planeswalkers that wipe boards and ramp into the commander.

strategy: Ramp through artifacts and lands toward casting [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] around turn 5.
Cast mana value 7 or greater colorless spells to trigger double cascade off [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]].
Assemble [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] for infinite colorless mana at no cost to activate.
Use Ugin planeswalkers and wipes like [[All Is Dust]] to clear colored threats while staying colorless.
Grind with Eldrazi value creatures like [[Thought-Knot Seer]] and [[Artisan of Kozilek]] to keep pressure up.

keep: [[Basalt Monolith]] plus a way to ramp into bigger threats keeps the plan moving.
Early ramp into a path toward casting the commander is a reasonable keep.
sendBack: Too many expensive spells and no cheap mana rocks stalls the whole plan.

tips.text: [[Basalt Monolith]] taps for three, and [[Forsaken Monument]] doubles that to six, letting you untap it repeatedly for free.
[[Omarthis, Ghostfire Initiate]] grows whenever you put counters on colorless creatures like [[Hangarback Walker]].
[[Ugin, the Ineffable]] reduces the cost of colorless spells, helping you hit mana value 7 for [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]]'s trigger sooner.

weaknesses: Moderate: The deck leans on artifacts like [[Sol Ring]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] with no answer to an opposing [[Vandalblast]] effect.
Moderate: Only 3 of 14 interaction pieces are instant speed, leaving [[Kozilek, the Great Distortion]]'s counter as a rare fast answer.
Minor: Removing [[Basalt Monolith]] before [[Forsaken Monument]] resolves denies the infinite mana line.

rendered.overview: This Naya deck ramps toward Dinosaur payoffs and [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]], which hits the battlefield with other Dinosaurs off combat damage. Enrage triggers from creatures like [[Polyraptor]] and [[Bellowing Aegisaur]] combine with [[Walking Ballista]] or [[Forerunner of the Empire]] to make infinite tokens or counters, closing games once the pieces land.

strategy: Ramp with lands and mana dorks to accelerate toward big Dinosaurs and [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]].
Land [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] around turn 7 and connect in combat to cascade Dinosaurs onto the battlefield.
Assemble [[Forerunner of the Empire]] with [[Polyraptor]] to make infinite tokens and damage triggers.
Use [[Bellowing Aegisaur]] with [[Walking Ballista]] to pile infinite +1/+1 counters onto your board.
Fall back on trampling attackers like [[Ghalta, Primal Hunger]] and [[Thrasta, Tempest's Roar]] if combos stall.

keep: [[Walking Ballista]] alongside early mana sets up the counter engine.
A hand with ramp and a way to keep casting creatures is solid.
sendBack: A hand missing red or white sources can't cast half this deck.
Too many lands with no path to Dinosaurs or ramp just sits still.

tips.text: [[Bellowing Aegisaur]] Enrage plus [[Walking Ballista]] pinging it lets counters snowball across your board.
[[Forerunner of the Empire]] damages Dinosaurs entering, which triggers [[Polyraptor]]'s Enrage to copy itself.
[[Marauding Raptor]] damaging [[Polyraptor]] as it enters triggers Enrage to make another copy.

keyCards.job: Combat damage puts free Dinosaurs onto the battlefield.
Finds Dinosaurs and damages them on entry.
Copies itself when damaged, fueling token loops.
Spreads +1/+1 counters when it takes damage.
Converts counters into repeatable damage output.

Fetches basics when Enrage triggers fire.

Moderate: With 0 instant-speed answers among its interaction, the deck can't stop a fast combo before [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] even attacks.

rendered.overview: [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] builds a wide army of Goblin tokens and turns them into damage through sacrifice outlets and anthem effects. The deck can assemble infinite creature tokens and infinite commander casts once [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] joins [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and [[Skirk Prospector]] on the battlefield, since sacrificing Goblins for mana lets you recast a free [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] over and over. Short of that, the plan is simply tapping [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] for a growing horde and swinging with haste enablers.

strategy: Ramp into [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] around turn 4 using mana rocks like [[Sol Ring]] and [[Arcane Signet]].
Tap [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] each turn to flood the board with Goblin tokens.
Assemble [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] with [[Skirk Prospector]] and [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] for infinite casts and tokens.
Grant haste with [[Goblin Chieftain]] or [[Bloodlust Inciter]] so new Goblins can attack immediately.
Finish with [[Goblin War Strike]] or combat damage once the board is wide enough.

keep: [[Skirk Prospector]] alongside a few lands sets up the sacrifice engine early.
Early ramp like [[Sol Ring]] backed by a path to [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] on turn 4.
sendBack: No early plays and no Goblins to fuel [[Goblin Bombardment]] later stalls out.

tips.text: [[Goblin Lookout]] can sacrifice a token to pump the team right after [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] makes a swarm.
[[Skirk Prospector]] sacrifices spare Goblins for mana to recast [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] if it dies.
[[Goblin Warchief]] reduces the cost of [[Dragon Fodder]] and gives the resulting tokens haste.
[[Pashalik Mons]] turns Goblins sacrificed to [[Tar Pitcher]] into extra damage from their deaths.

weaknesses: Critical: Losing [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] repeatedly removes the main token engine the deck is built around.
Moderate: The deck leans on enchantments like [[Goblin Bombardment]] and has no way to protect them from removal.
Moderate: The plan is mostly wide combat damage, so a fog or [[Goblin War Strike]]-stopping blocker wall can stall it out.

rendered.overview: [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] lead a Jeskai deck built around Gods, experience counters, and proliferate effects that grow +1/+1 counters until a wide board swings for lethal. [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] piles counters onto a creature each end step while [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] turns those experience counters into card draw and direct damage, and proliferate pieces like [[Inexorable Tide]] or [[Tezzeret's Gambit]] accelerate the counters even faster.

rendered.overview: [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] leads a mono-blue Wizards deck built around cheap instants and sorceries, countermagic, and card draw. The deck assembles [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] with [[Sublime Epiphany]] for infinite death, ETB, LTB and magecraft triggers once enough mana is online, and backs that up with steady counterspells and looting effects to reach the combo or just grind opponents out with Wizards tribal synergy.

strategy: Cast [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] around turn 2 to discount future instants and sorceries.
Deploy Wizards like [[Archmage of Runes]] and [[Azami, Lady of Scrolls]] to keep cards flowing.
Hold up countermagic such as [[Counterspell]] and [[Mana Leak]] to protect your board state.
Assemble [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] with [[Sublime Epiphany]] for infinite death, ETB, LTB and magecraft triggers.
If mana allows, loop [[Ghostly Flicker]] with [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] for infinite artifact and creature ETB/LTB value.

keep: [[Sol Ring]] into a cheap engine piece starts the plan.
Early [[Archmage of Runes]] backed by a way to draw more cards.
sendBack: A hand lacking any blue spells to cast can't function here.
Too many lands with no cheap interaction stalls the plan.

tips.text: Cast [[Sublime Epiphany]] then flash in [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] to copy it for its chosen modes repeatedly.
Use [[Ghostly Flicker]] to blink [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] along with an artifact for repeated enter-the-battlefield value.
Tap [[Azami, Lady of Scrolls]] off other Wizards like [[Patron Wizard]] to draw extra cards each turn.
[[Archmage of Runes]] and [[Jace's Sanctum]] both discount and reward casting instants and sorceries together.

Copies a spell, enabling the infinite combo.
Pairs with Naru Meha for infinite triggers.
Blinks Naru Meha for repeated ETB value.
Discounts spells and draws extra cards.
Taps Wizards to draw cards each turn.

weaknesses: Moderate: The deck has no way to deal with an opposing [[Null Rod]] shutting off its artifact mana.
Moderate: Removing [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] before it resolves with [[Sublime Epiphany]] stops the combo cold.
Minor: The deck lacks a fog or pillowfort effect like [[Ghostly Prison]] to stop aggressive attackers.

Unblockable threats like [[Changeling Outcast]], [[Tormented Soul]], and [[Slither Blade]] enable ninjutsu swaps into [[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]], [[Fallen Shinobi]], or [[Higure, the Still Wind]], while a stack of counterspells and cheap removal protects the attack plan.

rendered.overview: This Dimir deck uses [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] and a dense suite of cheap evasive creatures and Ninjas to ninjutsu in damage triggers, draining opponents off revealed cards while drawing extra cards along the way. Unblockable threats like [[Changeling Outcast]], [[Tormented Soul]], and [[Slither Blade]] enable ninjutsu swaps into [[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]], [[Fallen Shinobi]], or [[Higure, the Still Wind]], while a stack of counterspells and cheap removal protects the attack plan.

strategy: Play an evasive creature like [[Tormented Soul]] or [[Mist-Cloaked Herald]] to set up an unblocked attacker.
Use ninjutsu to swap in [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] or another Ninja for guaranteed combat damage.
Trigger [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] repeatedly to reveal cards and drain life while filling your hand.
Protect the attack with counterspells like [[Counterspell]] and [[Swan Song]] to stop removal and wraths.
Chain Ninjas such as [[Ingenious Infiltrator]] and [[Moon-Circuit Hacker]] for extra card draw off combat damage.

keep: [[Changeling Outcast]] plus a cheap counterspell sets up an early unblocked attack.
sendBack: A hand with no blue source struggles to cast [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] on time.
Too many expensive spells and no early unblockable creature stalls the plan.

tips.text: Bounce an unblocked [[Mistblade Shinobi]] to hand, then ninjutsu in [[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]] for a reanimation hit.
[[Prosperous Thief]] makes a Treasure off Ninja damage, helping cast [[Fallen Shinobi]] later that turn.
Use [[Mission Briefing]] to recast [[Reanimate]] from the graveyard for another reanimation target.

weaknesses: Moderate: [[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]] and [[Reanimate]] both rely on the graveyard, so [[Bojuka Bog]] style hate from an opponent can cut the plan off.
Moderate: Without [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] on board the life-drain engine stops, leaving only incidental Ninja triggers like [[Ninja of the Deep Hours]].
Minor: The deck has no dedicated answer to an opposing artifact or enchantment beyond a few counterspells like [[Negate]].

assessment.line: [[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]] and [[Reanimate]] both rely on the graveyard, so [[Bojuka Bog]] style hate from an opponent can cut the plan off.
The deck has no dedicated answer to an opposing artifact or enchantment beyond a few counterspells like [[Negate]].

The plan depends almost entirely on unblocked combat damage, so a fog like an opposing [[Ghostly Prison]] effect would stall it.
